481: /* Check if the specified command bit is set for the specified user.
482:  * The function returns 1 is the bit is set or 0 if it is not.
483:  * Note that this function does not check the ALLCOMMANDS flag of the user
484:  * but just the lowlevel bitmask.
485:  *
486:  * If the bit overflows the user internal representation, zero is returned
487:  * in order to disallow the execution of the command in such edge case. */
488: int ACLGetSelectorCommandBit(const aclSelector *selector, unsigned long id) {
489:     uint64_t word, bit;
490:     if (ACLGetCommandBitCoordinates(id,&word,&bit) == C_ERR) return 0;
491:     return (selector->allowed_commands[word] & bit) != 0;
492: }

494: /* When +@all or allcommands is given, we set a reserved bit as well that we
495:  * can later test, to see if the user has the right to execute "future commands",
496:  * that is, commands loaded later via modules. */
497: int ACLSelectorCanExecuteFutureCommands(aclSelector *selector) {
498:     return ACLGetSelectorCommandBit(selector,USER_COMMAND_BITS_COUNT-1);
499: }

501: /* Set the specified command bit for the specified user to 'value' (0 or 1).
502:  * If the bit overflows the user internal representation, no operation
503:  * is performed. As a side effect of calling this function with a value of
504:  * zero, the user flag ALLCOMMANDS is cleared since it is no longer possible
505:  * to skip the command bit explicit test. */
506: void ACLSetSelectorCommandBit(aclSelector *selector, unsigned long id, int value) {
507:     uint64_t word, bit;
508:     if (ACLGetCommandBitCoordinates(id,&word,&bit) == C_ERR) return;
509:     if (value) {
510:         selector->allowed_commands[word] |= bit;
511:     } else {
512:         selector->allowed_commands[word] &= ~bit;
513:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS;
514:     }
515: }

649: /* This function returns an SDS string representing the specified selector ACL
650:  * rules related to command execution, in the same format you could set them
651:  * back using ACL SETUSER. The function will return just the set of rules needed
652:  * to recreate the user commands bitmap, without including other user flags such
653:  * as on/off, passwords and so forth. The returned string always starts with
654:  * the +@all or -@all rule, depending on the user bitmap, and is followed, if
655:  * needed, by the other rules needed to narrow or extend what the user can do. */
656: sds ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules(aclSelector *selector) {
657:     sds rules = sdsempty();
658: 
659:     /* We use this fake selector as a "sanity" check to make sure the rules
660:      * we generate have the same bitmap as those on the current selector. */
661:     aclSelector *fake_selector = ACLCreateSelector(0);
662: 
663:     /* Here we want to understand if we should start with +@all or -@all.
664:      * Note that when starting with +@all and subtracting, the user
665:      * will be able to execute future commands, while -@all and adding will just
666:      * allow the user the run the selected commands and/or categories.
667:      * How do we test for that? We use the trick of a reserved command ID bit
668:      * that is set only by +@all (and its alias "allcommands"). */
669:     if (ACLSelectorCanExecuteFutureCommands(selector)) {
670:         rules = sdscat(rules,"+@all ");
671:         ACLSetSelector(fake_selector,"+@all",-1);
672:     } else {
673:         rules = sdscat(rules,"-@all ");
674:         ACLSetSelector(fake_selector,"-@all",-1);
675:     }
676: 
677:     /* Apply all of the commands and categories to the fake selector. */
678:     int argc = 0;
679:     sds *argv = sdssplitargs(selector->command_rules, &argc);
680:     serverAssert(argv != NULL);
681: 
682:     for(int i = 0; i < argc; i++) {
683:         int res = ACLSetSelector(fake_selector, argv[i], -1);
684:         serverAssert(res == C_OK);
685:     }
686:     if (sdslen(selector->command_rules)) {
687:         rules = sdscatfmt(rules, "%S ", selector->command_rules);
688:     }
689:     sdsfreesplitres(argv, argc);
690: 
691:     /* Trim the final useless space. */
692:     sdsrange(rules,0,-2);
693: 
694:     /* This is technically not needed, but we want to verify that now the
695:      * predicted bitmap is exactly the same as the user bitmap, and abort
696:      * otherwise, because aborting is better than a security risk in this
697:      * code path. */
698:     if (memcmp(fake_selector->allowed_commands,
699:                         selector->allowed_commands,
700:                         sizeof(selector->allowed_commands)) != 0)
701:     {
702:         serverLog(LL_WARNING,
703:             "CRITICAL ERROR: User ACLs don't match final bitmap: '%s'",
704:             rules);
705:         serverPanic("No bitmap match in ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules()");
706:     }
707:     ACLFreeSelector(fake_selector);
708:     return rules;
709: }

711: sds ACLDescribeSelector(aclSelector *selector) {
712:     listIter li;
713:     listNode *ln;
714:     sds res = sdsempty();
715:     /* Key patterns. */

718:     } else {
719:         listRewind(selector->patterns,&li);
720:         while((ln = listNext(&li))) {
721:             keyPattern *thispat = (keyPattern *)listNodeValue(ln);
722:             res = sdsCatPatternString(res, thispat);
723:             res = sdscatlen(res," ",1);
724:         }
725:     }

727:     /* Pub/sub channel patterns. */

731:         res = sdscatlen(res,"resetchannels ",14);

741:     /* Command rules. */

748: /* This is similar to ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules(), however instead of
749:  * describing just the user command rules, everything is described: user
750:  * flags, keys, passwords and finally the command rules obtained via
751:  * the ACLDescribeSelectorCommandRules() function. This is the function we call
752:  * when we want to rewrite the configuration files describing ACLs and
753:  * in order to show users with ACL LIST. */
754: robj *ACLDescribeUser(user *u) {
755:     if (u->acl_string) {
756:         incrRefCount(u->acl_string);
757:         return u->acl_string;
758:     }
759: 
760:     sds res = sdsempty();
761: 
762:     /* Flags. */
763:     for (int j = 0; ACLUserFlags[j].flag; j++) {
764:         if (u->flags & ACLUserFlags[j].flag) {
765:             res = sdscat(res,ACLUserFlags[j].name);
766:             res = sdscatlen(res," ",1);
767:         }
768:     }

770:     /* Passwords. */

772:     listNode *ln;
773:     listRewind(u->passwords,&li);
774:     while((ln = listNext(&li))) {
775:         sds thispass = listNodeValue(ln);
776:         res = sdscatlen(res,"#",1);
777:         res = sdscatsds(res,thispass);
778:         res = sdscatlen(res," ",1);

782:     listRewind(u->selectors,&li);
783:     while((ln = listNext(&li))) {
784:         aclSelector *selector = (aclSelector *) listNodeValue(ln);
785:         sds default_perm = ACLDescribeSelector(selector);

794:     u->acl_string = createObject(OBJ_STRING, res);

797: 
798:     return u->acl_string;
799: }

824:  * or similar to return back to the minimal memory usage (and checks to do)
825:  * for the user. */

828:     for (int j = 0; j < USER_COMMAND_BITS_COUNT; j++) {
829:         if (selector->allowed_firstargs[j]) {

843:      * this user, we have to allocate the first-args array. */
844:     if (selector->allowed_firstargs == NULL) {
845:         selector->allowed_firstargs = zcalloc(USER_COMMAND_BITS_COUNT * sizeof(sds*));
846:     }

848:     /* We also need to enlarge the allocation pointing to the
849:      * null terminated SDS array, to make space for this one.
850:      * To start check the current size, and while we are here
851:      * make sure the first-arg is not already specified inside. */
852:     long items = 0;
853:     if (selector->allowed_firstargs[id]) {
854:         while(selector->allowed_firstargs[id][items]) {

896: /* Set a selector's properties with the provided 'op'.
897:  *
898:  * +<command>   Allow the execution of that command.
899:  *              May be used with `|` for allowing subcommands (e.g "+config|get")
900:  * -<command>   Disallow the execution of that command.
901:  *              May be used with `|` for blocking subcommands (e.g "-config|set")
902:  * +@<category> Allow the execution of all the commands in such category
903:  *              with valid categories are like @admin, @set, @sortedset, ...
904:  *              and so forth, see the full list in the server.c file where
905:  *              the Redis command table is described and defined.
906:  *              The special category @all means all the commands, but currently
907:  *              present in the server, and that will be loaded in the future
908:  *              via modules.
909:  * +<command>|first-arg    Allow a specific first argument of an otherwise
910:  *                         disabled command. Note that this form is not
911:  *                         allowed as negative like -SELECT|1, but
912:  *                         only additive starting with "+".
913:  * allcommands  Alias for +@all. Note that it implies the ability to execute
914:  *              all the future commands loaded via the modules system.
915:  * nocommands   Alias for -@all.
916:  * ~<pattern>   Add a pattern of keys that can be mentioned as part of
917:  *              commands. For instance ~* allows all the keys. The pattern
918:  *              is a glob-style pattern like the one of KEYS.
919:  *              It is possible to specify multiple patterns.
920:  * %R~<pattern> Add key read pattern that specifies which keys can be read
921:  *              from.
922:  * %W~<pattern> Add key write pattern that specifies which keys can be
923:  *              written to.
924:  * allkeys      Alias for ~*
925:  * resetkeys    Flush the list of allowed keys patterns.
926:  * &<pattern>   Add a pattern of channels that can be mentioned as part of
927:  *              Pub/Sub commands. For instance &* allows all the channels. The
928:  *              pattern is a glob-style pattern like the one of PSUBSCRIBE.
929:  *              It is possible to specify multiple patterns.
930:  * allchannels              Alias for &*
931:  * resetchannels            Flush the list of allowed channel patterns.
932:  */
933: int ACLSetSelector(aclSelector *selector, const char* op, size_t oplen) {
934:     if (!strcasecmp(op,"allkeys") ||
935:                !strcasecmp(op,"~*"))
936:     {
937:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS;
938:         listEmpty(selector->patterns);
939:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"resetkeys")) {
940:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS;
941:         listEmpty(selector->patterns);
942:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"allchannels") ||
943:                !strcasecmp(op,"&*"))
944:     {
945:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCHANNELS;
946:         listEmpty(selector->channels);
947:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"resetchannels")) {
948:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCHANNELS;
949:         listEmpty(selector->channels);
950:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"allcommands") ||
951:                !strcasecmp(op,"+@all"))
952:     {
953:         memset(selector->allowed_commands,255,sizeof(selector->allowed_commands));
954:         selector->flags |= SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS;
955:         sdsclear(selector->command_rules);
956:         ACLResetFirstArgs(selector);
957:     } else if (!strcasecmp(op,"nocommands") ||
958:                !strcasecmp(op,"-@all"))
959:     {
960:         memset(selector->allowed_commands,0,sizeof(selector->allowed_commands));
961:         selector->flags &= ~SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLCOMMANDS;
962:         sdsclear(selector->command_rules);
963:         ACLResetFirstArgs(selector);
964:     } else if (op[0] == '~' || op[0] == '%') {
965:         if (selector->flags & SELECTOR_FLAG_ALLKEYS) {
966:             errno = EEXIST;
967:             return C_ERR;
968:         }
969:         int flags = 0;
970:         size_t offset = 1;
971:         if (op[0] == '%') {
